packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-02 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (first reader, images only)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification, author, work or earlier reading for this fragment. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001.jpg to image-010.jpg (plus one file-name listing of the packet folder to learn the image names; packet.json was not opened). No web, search, catalogue or edition was used.

Conventions: (..) = proposed expansion; ?word? = uncertain reading; [illegible] = not readable by me; [..] = lost to tear/hole; line numbers are counted from the top of the named image, counting partly cropped lines. The hand is a tiny, extremely abbreviated scholastic cursive in which most words are reduced to two or three letters with superscripts; expansions are therefore proposals, and many tokens are given as letter-shapes only.

------------------------------------------------------------
1. LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
------------------------------------------------------------
A narrow vertical strip of parchment, irregularly torn, photographed on both faces with a grey scale. A modern paper tab is attached at the top (on face B it carries a pencil note, apparently "3/" over "17" or similar - modern, not part of the text).

Face A: overview image-001; tiles image-002 (top), image-003, image-004, image-005 (bottom of text).
Face B: overview image-006; tiles image-007, image-008, image-009, image-010 (bottom of text). NOTE: the first four or five lines of face B are visible only in the overview image-006; no native-resolution tile covers them.

- Face A: about 24 lines. A wide blank area lies to the RIGHT of the text and a large blank area above and below; the LEFT side of the text block is torn away (except in two places where a tongue of parchment projects left, image-003 L2-L4 and image-005 L3-L6). So face A preserves line ends, and mostly not line beginnings. Text block is a single column on what survives.
- Face B: about 40 lines. A wide blank margin lies to the LEFT; line beginnings are preserved and line ends are lost to the tear on the right (again except for two projecting tongues, image-008 L1-L4 and image-010 L4-L9). Beyond the lower tongue, at the far right edge, are the first letters of lines of a SECOND column (image-010: "?sp..?", a large "C"-shaped paraph or initial, "?E..?"); so the page had at least two columns.
- No running title and no rubric in colour seen. Ink brown; face A lower lines are fainter/greyer.
- Enlarged initials / paragraph marks (observation): face A has "Jtem" written with a tall enlarged J twice (image-003 L7 and L10). Face B has an enlarged looped initial with a flag at the very top (overview only, "C"/"Co.."), a large "T"/"C"-like mark at image-007 L5, a paraph before "Ad" at image-009 L7, a boxed/penwork initial "S" at image-009 L11 (= image-010 L2), a paraph before image-010 L4, and a paraph inside the last line (image-010 L9).
- One interlinear addition on face A (image-003 L5, a short word above the line end) and one on face B (image-010 L8, a small "a" above the line). One struck-through word on face A (image-004 L8). Small superscript letters are everywhere but are abbreviation marks, not glosses.
- Dry-point or ink strokes in the left margin of face B near image-007 L5-L6 (two or three short oblique lines) - possibly a nota/tie mark; a dark blot beside them.
- Tentative interpretation: scholastic prose built of short argument units ("Item ...", "Ad aliam ...", "Solutio ..."-type openings), i.e. question-style or commentary-style material. I do not infer work or author. No lemma underlining is visible, so I cannot separate quoted lemmata from commentary.

------------------------------------------------------------
2. AREAS SELECTED / AREAS LEFT UNREAD
------------------------------------------------------------
Selected: all of face B covered by tiles (best ink), and all of face A. Left effectively unread: face B lines 1-5 (overview only), face A image-005 L2 and L5 (stain), the second-column traces on face B.
Suggested further views: a native-resolution tile of the top of face B; a wider view of whatever adjoins the right edge of face B / left edge of face A.

------------------------------------------------------------
3. FACE B (line beginnings preserved; line ends mostly lost)
------------------------------------------------------------
From the overview image-006 only (low confidence, letters a few pixels high):
image-006 (a) ?C..? [enlarged initial with flag] ?aut(em)? [..]
image-006 (b) ?diuisio? ?sillo..? [..]
image-006 (c) ?distinguit(ur)? ?mult..? [..]
image-006 (d) ?..nes? ?diuisio? ?aut(em)? [..]
(then the lines covered by image-007)

image-007 L1  [top cropped] ?..? ?diuis..? [..]
image-007 L2  ?..ta(li)? ?diffi(ni)c(io)? ?p(er)? [..]
image-007 L3  ?diffi(nici)o? ?p(er)? ?diue(rs)..? [..]
image-007 L4  ?p(ri)me? ?sc(ien)c(i)e? [..]             [a small superscript above the first word]
image-007 L5  ?T(er)cio? / ?C..? [large initial-like mark; blot and oblique strokes in the margin to its left] ?n(on)? ?sc..? [..]
image-007 L6  ?p(er)? ?quecu(m)q(ue)? / ?q(ui)ntam? [..]

image-009 L1-L2 repeat image-008 L10-L11 (overlap).
image-009 L3  ?in? ?g(e)n(er)e? ?s(ed)? ?o(mn)e? ?p(re)dica(bi)le? [space] ?s..? ?..? [..]
image-009 L4  ?diffe(re)n(ci)e? ?q(ua)le? [space] (et) ?n(on)? ?exist..? [..]

image-009 L7  [paraph] Ad ?Aliam? ad ?p(ri)mam? ?d(icen)d(u)m? ?(est)? [..]
image-009 L8  magnam difficultate(m) q(uia) ?..? [..]              ["magnam difficultatem quia" is clear]
image-009 L9  ?sc(ir)e? ?in? ?e(ss)e(n)c(i)a(m)? / ?..ciuate? ?logico? ?s(ed)? ?..? [..]      ["logico" or "logice" fairly clear]
image-009 L10 ?g(e)n(er)alissima(m)? (et) ?excluat? / ?exeunte? ?e..? [..]     [first word: long word ending -lissima(m), read as generalissima(m)]
image-009 L11 [boxed penwork initial] ?Soluta? / ?Solucio? (et) ?app(ar)e(n)c(i)a? ?in? ?p(ri)o(r)e? ?p(er)? ?s..? [..]
image-009 L12 [bottom cropped] ?..? ?alij? ?..? [..]

image-010 L1  repeats image-009 L10 (overlap).
image-010 L2  repeats image-009 L11: [boxed initial] ?Soluta? (et) ?app(ar)e(n)c(i)a? ?in? ?p(ri)o(r)e? ?p(er)? ?s..? [..]
image-010 L3  ?in? ?vice(m)? ?alij? ?d(i)c(u)nt? (et) ?in? ?c..? [hole] [..]
image-010 L4  [paraph] ?Ad? ?inuice(m)? ?vid(etur)? ?acc(ide)ntalia? ?sp(eci)ei? ?cad(un)t? [edge; beyond it the second-column trace "?sp..?"]
image-010 L5  ?(et)c? ?n(on)? ?s(ed)? ?in? ?vna? / ?diui(s)a? ?g(e)n(er)e? ?singil..? / ?si(mi)l(ite)r? [edge; second column: large "C" initial/paraph]
image-010 L6  [hole at left] ?hoc? ?istud? q(uia) ?eciam? ?..? de accide(n)tib(us)        ["de accidentibus" is clear]
image-010 L7  ?..ib(us)? (et) ?absolutis? ?n(on)? ?sc(ien)c(i)a? ?in? ?..? ?s(ed)? ?h(uius)mo(d)i?
image-010 L8  ?d(i)c(itu)r? (et) ?s(ed)? ?acc(ident)ia? [small "a" written above the line here] ?in? ?effectu(m)? ?..? ?difficile?
image-010 L9  ?sc(ien)c(i)a? ?q(ue)? ?in? ?p(er)? [paraph inside the line] ?..? ?aliam? ?su(n)t? ?d(i)c(t)a? ?p(er)d..?        [last line; a long descender from the paraph runs below; blank parchment beneath]
Second-column traces at the right edge of image-010 (L4-L9 level): "?sp..?", "C" (enlarged), "?..?", "?E..?" - line beginnings only.

Fairly secure on face B: "magnam difficultatem quia" (image-009 L8); "de accidentibus" (image-010 L6); a word in "-lissima(m)" at image-009 L10; repeated abbreviations for genus/species-type terms at image-008 L7-L8 and L11; "logic-" at image-009 L9; "Ad ... ad primam" opening at image-009 L7.

------------------------------------------------------------
4. FACE A (line ends preserved; line beginnings mostly lost)
------------------------------------------------------------
image-002 L1  [..] ?..? (et) ?s..? ?..? ?sc(ien)c(i)e?           [faint; first line of text; a reddish-brown smudge above it]
image-002 L2  [..] ?..? q(uia) ?in? ?h(oc)? ?..? ?p(ri)m(um)?
image-002 L3  [..] ?in? ?p(ri)ma? ?vnio(n)e? / ?diuisio(n)e? ?p(ro)? ?..? ?dice(re)t(ur)?
image-002 L4  [tongue at left] ?..? ?p(ri)m..? ?mi(n)or? q(uia) ?duo? ?..? ?p(er)? ?c(on)..?
image-002 L5  [bottom cropped; = image-003 L3]

image-003 L1-L2 repeat image-002 L3-L4 (overlap).
image-003 L3  ?..ctoru(m)? ?sp(eci)alissime? ?n(on)? ?p(ar)tit(ur)? [abraded gap] ?eade(m)? ?p(ro)..?       ["specialissime" fairly clear - long word with ss, ending -ime]
image-003 L4  ?..ia? ?mi(nor)? ?p(atet)? (et) ?s(e)c(un)da? ?sc(ilicet)? [abraded gap] ?..? ?c(on)ue(n)i(un)t?
image-003 L5  [..] ?..? ?sc(ilicet)? ?una? [gap] ?s(e)c(un)da? ?..? ?p(ri)us?        [a short word, ?sp(eci)e(s)? / ?diff(erenci)a?, added above the line end]
image-003 L6  [..] q(uia) ?sc(ilicet)? ?s(ed)? ?una? ?sp(eci)es? ?o(mn)i(n)o? ?in? ?p(ri)ma?
image-003 L7  [..] Jtem [enlarged J] ?hui(us)? (et) ?p(ro)? ?eade(m)? ?..?
image-003 L8  [..] ?app(ar)et? ?p(ri)ma? de ?alia? ?..? ?..?
image-003 L9  [..] ?diffe(re)n(ci)e? ?mi(nor)? ?s(e)c(un)da? ?s(ed)? ?p(ri)ma?
image-003 L10 [..] ?(et)c.? Jtem [enlarged J] ?in? ?n(atur)a? / ?nu(n)c? ?sc(ilicet)?
image-003 L11 [bottom cropped; = image-004 L2]

image-004 L1  repeats image-003 L10 (overlap): ?(et)c.? Jtem ?in? ?..? ?sc(ilicet)?
image-004 L2  [..] ?sp(eci)e(m)? ?..? ?alt(er)i(us)? . ?diu(er)si..?        [faint grey ink]
image-004 L3  [..] ?..? ?salte(m)? [gap] ?..? ?sp(eci)alissimu(m)?
image-004 L4  [..] ?de? ?q(ui)b(us)da(m)? ?sillo(gism)..? / ?sil(icet)? ?s(e)c(un)d(u)s?
image-004 L5  [..] ?q(uod)? ?p(re)dicat(ur)? ?sp(eci)alissimu(m)?
image-004 L6  [..] ?(et)? ?de? ?illo? ?diffe(re)ns? ?..? ?in? ?eo? ?q(uo)d?
image-004 L7  [..]?..ui? ?diuisiu(um)? [gap] ?..? ?de? ?plurib(us)?
image-004 L8  [..] ?..? ?d(icitu)r? [one word struck through with a horizontal stroke - visible deletion, unread] ?sillo(gis)mu(m)? / ?si(mi)l(ite)r? ?sp(eci)al(ite)r?
image-004 L9  [..] ?ille? ?sc(ien)c(i)e? ?n(on)? ?sc(ilicet)? ?diuisiue? ?..?
image-004 L10 [bottom cropped] ?..? ?p(ri)ma? ?..? ?..?

image-005 L1  repeats image-004 L9 (overlap).
image-005 L2  [..] ?..? ?p(ri)ma? ?s(ed)? ?..? ?..? [faint; = image-004 L10]
image-005 L3  [tongue at left] ?..? [stain] ?..? ?alie? ?sc(ien)c(i)e? ?s(e)c(un)d(u)m? / ?seq(ui)t(ur)? ?p(re)dic..?
image-005 L4  ?mo(do)? ?n(on)? ?..ca..? ?s(ed)? ?app(aret)? ?..?         [stained]
image-005 L5  [illegible - brown stain/adhesive residue over the whole line; isolated strokes only]
image-005 L6  ?dialetico(rum)? et ?sophista(rum)? / ?sophistic..?       [short last line, ending mid-line with a long horizontal flourish further right; "et soph-" fairly clear; blank parchment below]

Fairly secure on face A: "Jtem" twice with enlarged J; a word read as "specialissim-" three times (image-003 L3, image-004 L3 and L5); the last line "... et sophist-" preceded by a word in "-ticorum/-ecticorum".

------------------------------------------------------------
5. LIMITATIONS
------------------------------------------------------------
- This is an unverified image reading. Because every line on both faces is truncated on one side by the tear, no line gives a complete clause; expansions could not be controlled by syntax and I have not tried to supply the lost halves.
- The abbreviation system is extreme (many words are one letter plus superscript). Where I give an expansion with question marks it is one of several the strokes allow. Tokens I rendered "sc(ilicet)", "s(ed)", "sc(ien)c(i)e", "s(e)c(un)da" in particular share very similar shapes and may be confused with one another.
- Top of face B (four or five lines, including an enlarged initial) is seen only in the reduced overview; readings (a)-(d) there are guesses at word shape.
- Face A image-005 L5 is under a stain; image-004 L2-L7 are in faint grey ink.
- Which face is recto, and the relation of the two columns glimpsed on face B, cannot be settled from these images. Line numbering counts partly cropped lines at tile tops; overlaps between consecutive tiles are flagged and are not additional text.
- I did not attempt to identify the work or author and supplied no words from memory of any text. I did nothing beyond the stated rules other than the single file-name listing mentioned at the top.
